FrameBlock.description:
A run of consecutive pitch frames, as columns: frame `k` of the block sits at sample frame
`start + k·hop`, and has `pitch[k]`, `voicing[k]` and `level[k]`. The three columns have one
length.

level.description: Each frame's level: the root mean square of its integration window.

pitch.description:
Each frame's fundamental, in the head's unit to 0.1, or `null` where the smoothed track
says the frame is unvoiced.

start.description: The sample frame the block's first frame sits at, on the take's timeline.

voicing.description: Each frame's own voicing probability, before smoothing.

PerformanceHead.description: What every frame of a performance shares: the first line's head.

first_frame.description:
The sample frame the first pitch frame sits at, on the take's timeline at `rate`: the
middle of its integration window.

hop.description: Sample frames from one pitch frame to the next.

rate.description: The analysis rate, in Hz: what every frame number counts.

take.description:
The audio the frames were read from: its decoded samples' digest, with their own rate,
channel count and length, as the analysis read from it states it. Added in `performance`
1.1; absent before, meaning not stated. The stage leaves it absent, since a take's digest
is known only once all of it is read: the capture command fills it.

PitchUnit.description: The pitch unit a performance is written in.

oneOf.description:
Absolute cents, `1200·log2(hz/440) + 6900`: MIDI's numbering at 100 a key, so 6900.0 is
440 Hz and 6907.9 is 442 Hz. A unit, not a reading: it maps one-to-one onto Hz, and is
never rounded to a key.

Take.description:
The audio an analysis was read from: its samples' digest, and their rate, channel count and
length, as decoded.

channels.description: The source's channel count, before any downmix.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of the decoded samples ([`TakeDigest`]).

frames.description: The take's length in frames (one sample per channel) at `rate`, a filled gap included.

rate.description: The source's own sample rate, in Hz, before any resampling.

TakeDigest.description: The SHA-256 of a take's decoded samples: the bytes `duet-take-1`, the rate as a little-endian u32, the channel count as a little-endian u16, then every sample, interleaved, as the little-endian bits of its f32.
